THE LIGHT CAFÉ · SCIENTIFIC BACKGROUND

The Light Café: a field study of morning light.

As the days grow shorter, we get less daylight. Morning light can help us get the day started. At the Light Café in Tübingen, you can experience light and discover our research into the body clock, sleep and attention.

01 / THE RESEARCH QUESTION

How does morning light
affect circadian timing?

How do light intensity and spectral composition shape the human circadian response in everyday settings?

The Light Café is a field study combining controlled morning light exposure with circadian, behavioural and subjective outcome measures. It asks how responses vary across light conditions and between individuals.

The mobile research trailer at Europaplatz, by Tübingen’s main railway station, serves as both an intervention space and a meeting place for researchers and the public. The Light Café opens on 19 November 2026; the study phase begins on 30 November 2026.

The long-term aim is to inform biologically grounded, more personalised light interventions. These are research objectives, not established outcomes of this project.

02 / STUDY DESIGN

The study
at a glance.

Sequential cohorts with light conditions
adapted in response to previous observations.

10weekday sessions
per participant
60minutes per session
over two weeks
144–192target participants
across 6–8 cohorts
  1. BASELINE

    Baseline
    measurements

    Assess circadian phase with dim-light melatonin onset (DLMO), alongside actigraphy and cognitive performance measures.

  2. INTERVENTION

    Morning light
    sessions

    Ten one-hour sessions on weekdays, within four daily time windows between 07:00 and 11:00. Light intensity and spectral composition are controlled.

  3. FOLLOW-UP

    Repeat assessments
    and analyse the data.

    Repeat the assessments and collect subjective tiredness and well-being measures. Analyse each cohort to inform subsequent light conditions.

The recruitment target is up to six participants per time window and up to 24 per cohort. The sample range is an operational recruitment estimate, not a reported power calculation or an achieved sample. Exact light settings, eligibility criteria, allocation procedures and adaptation rules are not yet specified here.

03 / OUTCOME DOMAINS

What we
measure.

Circadian, behavioural
and subjective measures.

Circadian phase DLMO
Timing of the evening rise in melatonin under dim-light conditions, measured before and after the intervention.
Sleep and activity ACTIGRAPHY
Objective assessment of rest–activity patterns using a wearable sensor.
Cognition PERFORMANCE
Tasks assessing cognitive performance and attention alongside the physiological measurements.
Daily experience SELF-REPORT
Subjective tiredness and well-being following the intervention.

Research and
public engagement

Visit the Light Café to experience light and get to know our research.

The public drop-in takes place on Friday, 20 November, and Monday–Friday, 23–27 November 2026, from 07:00 to 11:00 each day at Europaplatz, Tübingen. Visitors can attend this open programme before the study phase.

Three talks with Manuel Spitschan accompany the programme: 24 November 2026, 18:00–19:00 at Werkstadthaus in Tübingen; 1 December 2026, 13:00–14:00 online via Zoom; and 4 December 2026, 15:30–17:00 at the Hirsch-Begegnungsstätte, Hirschgasse 9, Tübingen. All three talks are in German. Event details, registration and flyers ↗

Our Lunch Bytes talk on 1 December is part of Mental Health Days 2026. Explore the full programme on the University of Tübingen website (in German) ↗
